earlier_scan.source_named: Yusop, Mohd. Sharifudin. 2013 (pp. 96-172, per Glottolog) on Orang Kanaq; also McDowell & Anderbeck 2020 on southern-peninsula Malay lects. Neither reachable online

sources.citation: McDowell, Jonathan & Karl Anderbeck. 2020. The Malay Lects of Southern Sumatra. JSEALS Special Publication. University of Hawai'i Press.
sources.note: Open access but eVols could not be reached by automated download; Glottolog's classification reference for Kanaq - check whether it says anything substantive about Kanaq (probably not).

sources.citation: Shahidi A.H., Nor Azwahanum Nor Shaid, Mohd Sharifudin Yusop, Marlyna Maros & Rahim Aman. 2018. Fenomena sosiobudaya Orang Asli Kanaq dalam penguasaan bahasa Melayu: satu tinjauan awal. e-Bangi 15(5): 146-156.
sources.note: No stress statement; sociolinguistic/educational study. Only an impressionistic remark that Kanaq words differ little from Malay but are pronounced 'agak cepat dan keras' (rather fast and hard).

sources.citation: Anderbeck, Karl. 2012. The Malayic-speaking Orang Laut: Dialects and directions for research. Wacana 14(2): 265-312. DOI 10.17510/wacana.v14i2.64
sources.note: Nothing for Kanaq: Orang Kanaq is listed under 'Data limitations' as a known group with no data ('No data from some known groups like Orang Seletar and Orang Kanaq (former Sea Tribe from around Batam, resettled in Johor)'); the phonological discussion (penult vowel changes etc.) concerns Riau Orang Laut lects only. Cites Yusof 2006 UKM PhD thesis on Duano and Kanaq, which the author had not seen.

sources.note: No phonology; reference lists harvested (Omar bin Abdul 1978, 1985 ethnographies; Collins 1989; Carey 1976; Yusop 2006/2008/2013).

sources.citation: Mohd Sharifudin Yusop. 2011. Ciri leksikal dialek Kanaq [Lexical characteristics of the Kanaq dialect]. Jurnal Linguistik (Persatuan Linguistik Malaysia) 13: 1-21.

tone.summary: No statement on tone or word prosody; the article covers only segmental phonology (7 vowels, 19 consonants, diphthongs, clusters) and word structure of Kanaq and four sister Proto-Malay lects.

sources.citation: Yusop, Mohd. Sharifudin. 2013. Keterancaman bahasa Orang Asli Duano dan Kanaq. Serdang: Universiti Putra Malaysia Press. xii+337 pp. ISBN 9789673443437. (Kanaq: pp. 96-172)

sources.note: The only work Glottolog tags as phonology+wordlist for Orang Kanaq (Glottolog's fullest description is a phonology or text collection); if any published statement on Kanaq word stress ('tekanan') exists it is here. HathiTrust coo.31924122761749 is search-only (Cornell copy) - a HathiTrust full-text search for 'tekanan'/'suku kata praakhir' from an unblocked host would tell in one minute whether the pages are worth an ILL scan.

sources.note: Lexical description of the Kanaq dialect from ethnographic fieldwork; search snippet: the Kanaq dialect 'has never before been documented and due to 82 native speakers left, the dialect is at a very critical stage'. Likely gives transcription conventions and sound correspondences with Standard Malay alongside the lexicon; no tone content expected (Malayic lect); whether it remarks on stress/intonation is unknown. Basis: title + search snippet.
